title: Prompt parse accelerator: harmonize kernel selection & lightweight pre-tokenizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The prefill/prompt preprocessing stack is a measurable CPU and latency hotspot for short-lived requests. Current path performs full UTF-8 normalization, full tokenization and heavyweight metric emission on the hot path, and we frequently pick suboptimal kernels downstream because the runtime lacks early signal about sequence-length distribution and character set.

Goal: Reduce prefill-side CPU overhead and end-to-end latency for common short prompt patterns (user queries, system prompts) while preserving tokenization fidelity for long or non-ASCII inputs. Target 40-60% reduction in prefill CPU and 20-30% median end-to-end latency improvement for 1-32 token prompts at 2048 context models.

Hypothesis: A lightweight, staged pre-tokenizer that emits early hints (ascii_only, avg_token_estimate, short_prefix_hash) combined with a kernel-hinting API into the scheduler will enable cheaper fast-paths (vectorized ASCII split + single-pass normalizer) and allow the attention runtime to pick fused small-sequence kernels. Speculative KV-cache warmup for repeated short prefixes will further reduce decode latency for bursty sessions.

Proposed approach:
  - Implement a micro pre-tokenizer (C++), opt-in, that applies a fast ascii-only code path and returns: ascii_only boolean, estimated_token_count, small_prefix_digest. This runs in ~50-200us for short strings.
  - Extend kernel_selection API to accept prefill hints (sequence_estimate, ascii_fastpath) and expose a low-cost heuristic in the scheduler to choose between fused small-seq attention kernels or regular kernels.
  - Add a tiny hotpath cache keyed by small_prefix_digest (TTL ~30s, size cap ~8k entries) to short-circuit full tokenization for repeated requests in the same session. Cache stores tokenized prefix and decoded token ids.
  - Introduce an affinity-aware decode scheduler tweak: prioritize requests flagged as "short_low_latency" to a lower-latency GPU queue (smaller batch targets, lower queueing) while preserving throughput for bulk workloads.

Success metrics: CPU cycles spent in prefill stage (p50/p95), median end-to-end latency for short prompts, cache hit rate, no regressions in tokenization correctness (roundtrip tests).
acceptance_criteria: Pre-tokenizer integrated behind feature flag and runnable in host; default off for safety
At least 40% reduction in prefill CPU cycles (p50) for 1-32 token short prompts in internal benchmark harness compared to baseline
Median end-to-end latency improvement >= 20% for short prompts at 2048 context model in our end-to-end harness
No tokenization mismatches in the canonical test corpus (including multi-byte unicode and edge cases)
Kernel selection honors prefill hints for >= 90% of short prompt test cases in CI
Hotpath cache hit-rate >= 15% on production-like replay dataset without memory blowup
Feature flag allows A/B rollback and is documented in release notes
perf_results: Bench (local harness v2) for 1-16 token queries on A100: baseline prefill CPU p50=1.9ms, p95=4.7ms. With pretokenizer + ascii fastpath: p50=0.8ms (58% reduction), p95=2.1ms. End-to-end median latency improved from 28ms to 18ms for short prompts when routed to small-seq fused kernels. Hotpath cache observed 18% hit rate on replay dataset with 8k TTL entries.
implementation_notes: Step 1: Add micro pre-tokenizer module in runtime/ingest; C++ with a single-header fast path for ascii detection
Step 2: Create kernel_hint struct in scheduler API (sequence_estimate:int, ascii_fastpath:bool, prefix_digest:16-byte) and wire through GRPC headers for private deployments
Step 3: Implement small_prefix_digest cache with LRU and TTL; baseline memory cap at 64MB per shard
Step 4: Modify kernel selector to prefer small-seq fused attention kernels when sequence_estimate <= threshold (configurable) and ascii_fastpath=true
Step 5: Add decode scheduler affinity: new low-latency queue with batch target 4-8 and aggressive dispatching; keep metrics and auto-scale knobs
Step 6: End-to-end tests, fuzz unicode edge cases, run regression suite and perf harness
Step 7: Gradual rollout: internal opt-in -> canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 100% with kill switch
risks: Tokenization divergence for edge unicode cases if pretokenizer shortcut used incorrectly
Hotpath cache might leak sensitive prefixes—ensure we only store token IDs and not raw prompt text, and encrypt in-memory if configured
Kernel hinting can cause misrouted requests if estimate is wrong leading to latency spikes under heavy load
Increased scheduler complexity may impact maintainability and require additional observability
